# dtcloud_image_versions (Data Source)

Reads the platform's own image catalogue.

This is not the same list as `dtcloud_images`. That one is what the image service holds; this one is
the curated set the platform offers, and it is the only place that says which flavors an image may
be built on.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The platform's curated catalogue -- not the same list as dtcloud_images, and
# the only place that says which flavors an image may be built on.
data "dtcloud_image_versions" "ubuntu" {
  type = "ubuntu"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `type` (String) Only return entries in this family, e.g. `ubuntu`. Applied by the provider; the endpoint takes no parameters.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `versions` (List of Object) Catalogue entries, sorted by family and then by version. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--versions))

<a id="nestedatt--versions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `versions`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String)
- `image_type` (String)
- `min_volume_size` (Number)
- `type` (String)
- `valid_flavor_ids` (List of String)
- `version` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **A sorted list, not a map.** The endpoint groups entries by family. They are flattened into one
  list and sorted by family and then by version, so a new catalogue entry does not reshuffle a plan.
  A new family can still shift the indexes after it, so filter with `type` and match on `version`
  rather than indexing into the full list.
* **`type` is applied by the provider** and ignores case; the endpoint takes no parameters.
* **An empty `valid_flavor_ids` means no restriction.** The catalogue field is untyped, and a list, a
  comma-separated string or a single value are all read back as a list.
